cohort: The study included 43 pregnant patients with pregnancy-associated colorectal cancer (pCRC) treated at the National Cancer Center/Cancer Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, between 1999 and 2023.
finding: Early-stage diagnosis and timely treatment significantly improved maternal survival and fetal outcomes in pregnant patients with CRC, while poorly differentiated tumors exhibited worse outcomes.
gest_age: Gestational age at diagnosis was found to influence fetal outcomes, with outcomes varying based on early, mid, or late pregnancy diagnoses.
